sentences.text: The petitioner in Crl.M.C.No.4791/2025 is the 2 nd accused and the petitioners in Crl.M.C.No.8629/2025 are the accused 3 to 5 in S.C. No.5/2025 on the file of the Special Court for PMLA cases/CBI-I, Ernakulam, which has arisen from ECIR/KCZO/25/2020 registered by the 1 st respondent for the predicate offence under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).

entities.text: Special Court for PMLA cases/CBI-I, Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
As the petitioners are the accused in the same crime, these Crl.M.Cs are being disposed of by this common order.
2.
The common case of the petitioners is that, the above crime was registered by the 1st respondent on the allegations that the accused persons have committed money laundering.

On the said allegations, Crime No. VC 4/2019 is registered by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau, Special Investigation Unit-I, 2025:KER:84087 CRL.MC Nos. 4791 & 8629 OF 2025 Thiruvananthapuram,
alleging commission of the offences under Section 120B, 409 and 420 of the IPC and Section 13(2)
r/w Section 13 (1) (d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act,1988.

3. The petitioners contend that they were not granted an opportunity of being heard, before taking cognizance of the said offence, as envisaged under the first proviso to Section 223(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 ('BNSS', for short) and as per the principles laid down by this Court in Saji John v. Assistant Director, Directorate of Enforcement [2025 KHC 819], Therefore, the entire proceedings leading to taking cognizance of offence are vitiated and are liable to be quashed.
4.

entities.text: Saji John v. Assistant Director, Directorate of Enforcement [2025 KHC 819]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have heard the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondents.

5. The learned Standing Counsel for the respondents 2025:KER:84087 CRL.MC Nos. 4791 & 8629 OF 2025 fairly submits that the petitioners were not granted an opportunity of being heard as per the mandate under Section 223(1) of the BNSS before taking cognizance of the offence.
In light of the above submission, these Crl.M.Cs are allowed, by setting aside the order taking cognizance of the offence.
Accordingly, the Trial Court is directed to reconsider the matter after affording the petitioners an opportunity of being heard as envisaged under Section 223(1) of the BNSS.
These Crl.M.Cs are disposed of accordingly.

SD/-
